card.name: Tambu
card.tagline: The 'Curacao blues' - Afro-Curacaoan drum, song and dance
card.profile: Tambu is the Afro-Curacaoan drum, song and dance complex, sometimes called 'the Curacao blues,' that emerged among enslaved Africans (largely from the Kongo/Angola region) under Dutch rule from the early 17th century. Per Wikipedia and ethnomusicologist Nanette de Jong, it centres on the tambu barrel drum and the chapi (hoe blade) struck as iron percussion, with call-and-response singing between a kantado and chorus over a 12/8 pulse. The accompanying dance is earthy and hip-driven yet governed by strict etiquette forbidding partners to touch; it was long banned by the Catholic Church and colonial government.
card.insight: Tambu is a vessel of Afro-Curacaoan memory and resistance - repressed for centuries by the Church and 1930s permit laws, it survives as a core expression of identity (Indiana University Press / Nanette de Jong; Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: The Curacao blues; hips that defied the ban. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Curacao.
